About the Organization
Hope Women’s Centerprovides a safe haven for at-risk women and teen girls across Arizona to get back on their feet. Our mission is to engage, encourage, and equip vulnerable women and teen girls by providing support for their physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. Get stories of impact straight in your inbox! To better serve women in crisis, Hope Women’s Center is expanding its reach across Arizona through ourHope on the Roadmobile program.

Read Better Be Better

Sophie Allen-Etchart — Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
Read Better Be Better's mission is to connect young readers and youth leaders to inspire a love of literacy and learning. Mission: Read Better Be Better is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Phoenix, Arizona, founded in 2014 as a response to thestate’s literacy crisis. Our mission is to equip youth with the skills to read and lead. This begins byaddressing the challenge that many 3rd graders in Arizona face, with a significant portion reading below grade level. This gap in reading proficiency often hinders their ability to transition from“learning to read” to “reading to learn” by 4th grade, impacting their academic progress and future opportunities. We believe that literacy is foundational to success in education and life, making our work vital in ensuring that every child has the opportunity to excel. Initially starting as an afterschool reading comprehension and leadership program pairing 3rd grade readers with middle school leaders, we have expanded our reach.Today, we serve students from kindergarten through 12th gradewith our continuum of programs, called the “Changemaker Continuum.”We have added two more programs over the years to further the high school students’ leadership skills: thePathways to Education Professions Program, providing high schoolers with experience in education professions by engaging with students in a classroom setting in one of our K-8 after-school literacy programs, and thePathways to Civic Leadership Program, guiding high school...

Teach For America Phoenix

Lauren Arndt — Executive Director
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
Our corps members and alumni work relentlessly every day with our communities to ensure the students of Arizona have the opportunities they deserve. Teach For America finds, develops, and supports leaders to expand opportunity for all children. Mission: What Is Leadership? It’s a Practice, Not a Position Join the TFA corps: a two-year, full-time teaching and leadership opportunity. Join TFA Ignite: a part-time, paid virtual tutoring role for current college students. Explore career events, hear from alumni, and sharpen your skills. Teach For America is a national network of leaders working to expand access to opportunity for students—starting in the classroom.We all remember the educators who shaped us. At TFA, that impact goes both ways: teaching transforms students, teachers, and tutors alike.

Valley Leadership

Dave Brown — Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
Driven to do: Valley Leadership empowers, leverages and mobilizes leaders to meaningfully impact the most pressing issues facing Arizona. About Valley Leadership Our Mission Valley Leadership empowers, leverages and mobilizes leaders... Mission: Valley Leadership empowers, leverages and mobilizes leaders to meaningfully impact the most pressing issues facing Arizona. A broad spectrum of Arizonans working together to impact the issues that matter most, setting the example on leadership. At our core, Valley Leadership builds community. We do that by empowering a broad spectrum of Arizonans to lead through our leadership programs and activating them to make a difference on our state’s most pressing issues through Impact Maker. Our work is grounded in thePrinciples of Doing®leadership framework, which shapes how we develop leaders and engage communities across Arizona. ThePrinciples of Doing®leadership frameworkdraws on the actions and values of the people who have made the greatest impact on our state throughout our history. With an emphasis on action, ourPrinciples of Doing®guide how Valley Leadership develops leaders through our programs and Impact Maker work, and how we engage our network to move Arizona forward.

Boys and Girls Club of Greater Scottsdale

Ivan Gilreath — President and Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
When school is out, we are in. We offer a variety of engaging programs to help your child reach their full potential. What we do to provide safe, enriching youth programs. Discover our commitment to youth development, programs and community engagement. Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Scottsdale serves thousands of youth at nine locations within Scottsdale, North Phoenix, Fountain Hills, the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community, and the Hualapai Nation. Inside our doors, youth development professionals and mentors provide guidance, support, and encouragement in a safe environment to create an optimal Club experience. Our outcome-based programming assures that success is within reach for all kids and teens, no matter their circumstances. To enable all young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential as productive, caring, responsible citizens. Provide a world-class Club Experience that assures success is within reach of every young person who enters our doors, with all members on track to graduate from high school with a plan for the future, demonstrating good character and citizenship, and living a healthy lifestyle. ACCOUNTABILITYWe uphold punctuality and accountability by consistently meeting deadlines, holding others accountable when needed, and fostering a culture of personal responsibility through transparent communication for continuous improvement.

Valley of the Sun United Way

Carla Vargas Jasa — President and Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
Valley of the Sun United Way monitors needs, identifies critical social issues and brings the right people together to advance the common good. We envision a community where every child, family and individual is healthy, has a safe place to live, and has every opportunity to succeed. Valley of the Sun United Way is part of a global network for community action. We bring people and resources together to tackle our communities’ toughest challenges. Valley of the Sun United Way envisions a community where every child, family, and individual is healthy, has a safe place to live, and has every opportunity to succeed in school, at work, and in life. As we celebrate 100 years of impact, we continue to unite the Valley around urgent needs and long-term solutions that strengthen Maricopa County. We address community needs through four focus areas: Housing and Homelessness, Health and Hunger, Education, and Workforce Development. We support the delivery of programs and provide direct services in Maricopa County to empower local residents. Valley of the Sun United Way sits at the center of our community ecosystem, bringing together organizations and partners to tackle complex challenges that no single organization can solve alone.

Bryan Madden — President
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
The Y is for EVERYONE. The Valley of the Sun YMCA is not only one of the oldest nonprofits in the state of Arizona, but we are also one of the largest. The Valley of the Sun YMCA needs your help to provide financial assistance to the most vulnerable populations in our community. Donate today! When you give to the YMCA, you’re not just making a donation; you’re creating real impact, opportunity, and hope across Arizona. Your generosity fuels programs that uplift our neighbors, helping individuals and families build safer, stronger futures and reach their full potential. As a nonprofit organization, we rely on the kindness of donors like you to make this mission possible. Together, we can build a more connected, supportive, and resilient community, one person, one family at a time. Thank you for helping us make a lasting difference. Community Connector:You help people who feel isolated find connection, belonging, and support through YMCA programs. Childcare Supporter:You make affordable, high-qualitychildcareavailable for working families and children.

Boys & Girls Club of the Valley

Marcia Mintz — Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
Boys & Girls Clubs of the Valley offers affordable after-school and summer programs for 20,000+ young people in grades K-12. At 30 Clubs across the Valley, BGCAZ provides award-winning programs designed to change the lives of young people. There is a reason Boys & Girls Clubs of the Valley (BGCAZ) is the largest childcare provider in the Valley: Parents trust BGCAZ to provide a safe, positive, fun environment for their kids’ out-of-school time. Explore one of our Boys & Girls Clubs of the Valley and see how BGCAZ can exceed your expectations for out-of-school-time care. Mission: Boys & Girls Clubs of the Valley empowers young people, especially those who need us most, to reach their full potential as productive, caring, responsible members of the community. There is a reason Boys & Girls Clubs of the Valley (BGCAZ) is the largest childcare provider in the Valley: Parents trust BGCAZ to provide a safe, positive, fun environment for their kids’ out-of-school time. To be the premier out-of-school-time provider and leading voice for youth development in Arizona, ensuring youth and teens have the skills and resilience to successfully navigate childhood and prepare for adulthood. Boys & Girls Clubs employs aFormula For Impactfor how the organization impacts the life of a child. Our programs are organized around fourPriority Outcomes: Academic Success, Health & Well-Being, Character & Leadership and Life & Workforce Readiness.

Andy Price — Scout Executive and Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
About Scouting Arizona, Grand Canyon Council The Boy Scouts of America (BSA), was incorporated on February 8, 1910, and chartered by Congress in 1916. Its purpose is to provide young adults an effective educational program designed to build desirable qualities of character, to train in the responsibilities of participating citizenship and to develop in them personal fitness. Community groups such as religious, educational, civic, fraternal, business, labor, governmental bodies, corporations, professional associations, and groups of citizens who have compatible goals and utilize the program provided accomplish the purpose by the Boy Scouts of America on the local level. The mission of Grand Canyon Council is to strengthen and expand Scouting in Arizona by building strong units, empowering leaders, and delivering programs and camps that enrich the local Scouting experience. Together, volunteer and professional Scouters create an environment where every young person can discover their path, live the ideals of the Scout Oath, Law, and Motto, and grow into the best version of themselves.

About the Organization
Valle Del Sol Community Health offers integrative and comprehensive medical care and health services in Phoenix and Mesa. Keep your entire family healthy with services ranging from primary care to behavioral health under one roof. Contact us today! Learn about Valle Del Sol Community Health, a nonprofit FQHC serving Phoenix and Mesa since 1970, founded by civil rights activists. Contact us to learn more! Mission: Our work is rooted in compassion, equity, and community empowerment: Valle Del Sol Community Health is a federally qualified health center (FQHC) and nonprofit community health organization dedicated to transforming lives across the greater Phoenix Valley. For more than 50 years, we've provided integrated medical and behavioral health services to adults, children, seniors, and families from all backgrounds. We offer comprehensive care under one roof: primary care, pediatrics, women's health, behavioral health, substance use recovery, psychiatry, and wellness services. Our team delivers culturally centered, bilingual care that treats the whole person. We alsoaccept most insurance plansand offersliding-fee supportbased on income to ensure cost is not a barrier to care. We provide care that honors the diverse traditions, languages, and experiences of the people we serve. John Swagert — Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
Mountain Park Center offers comprehensive, community-based affordable healthcare services for everyone in your family in the greater Phoenix area. Learn about Mountain Park Health Center—providing affordable, compassionate care to our diverse community through a team-based, patient-centered approach. Mountain Park Health Center is a nonprofit community health center. For more than 40 years we have been providing whole-patient care for the entire family. Each year we keep nearly 115,000 of our neighbors in Goodyear, Glendale, Tempe, and Phoenix healthy. Mountain Park believes in being proactive about your health. We know that health education, screenings and access to affordable medications help prevent serious health problems. Proactive healthcare can also help manage chronic conditions, like obesity and diabetes, and detect diseases in the most treatable stages. We are here for you anytime you need. Our caring staff is here to help you navigateAHCCCSor the health insurance marketplace. We can also help you apply forSNAP(formerly called food stamps) andTANF(cash assistance). If you don’t have health insurance, we will work with you to make healthcare affordable through ourSliding Fee Discount Programand other resources. We always put our patients first. As a Patient Centered Medical Home, Mountain Park offers all the care you need in one single place. You’ll have access to an entire Care Team of primary care physicians, physician’s assistants, nurse practitioners, clinical...

Child Crisis Arizona

Torrie Taj — Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
Child Crisis Arizona provides children and families with a safe environment, crisis support, and education to build strong, stable futures. Explore our programs in foster care, adoption, early education, and family resources. Child Crisis Arizona provides emergency shelter, foster care, adoption, counseling, early education, and parenting support services to Arizona’s most vulnerable children, youth and families. Our mission is to provide children and youth in Arizona a safe environment, free from abuse and neglect, by creating strong and successful families.

Terros Health

Karen Hoffman Tepper — President and Chief Executive Officer
✓ Scraped Visit Website
About the Organization
Terros Health — making healthcare more accessible and affordable for all. Comprehensive Care with a Personal Touch. At Terros Health, we are a team united in a desire to help patients become the best versions of themselves while creating healthy communities. We foster a culture where our team members feel seen, supported and appreciated, so every person we serve receives that same level of compassion and respect. Everyone deserves access to quality health care. It’s why we meet people where they are — virtually, in the community or at our health and counseling centers across the Valley and throughout the state. Walk-ins are always welcome. Once patients are here, we leave no stone unturned in helping them get comprehensive, compassionate care. Find out how we are living our mission of serving others at work and in the community.
